draft.title: Minor and major decisions
card: Minor decision
A choice that costs little and is easy to undo, such as what to buy for lunch or which pens to use.
Major decision
A choice that costs a lot, affects you for years and is hard to undo, such as buying a car or a home.
A mistake on a minor decision is cheap to fix. A mistake on a major decision can be costly and hard to reverse.
Because of this, a major decision needs planning. You compare options, work out the costs and think about the years ahead.
draft.remember: The bigger the cost and the harder to undo, the more planning a decision needs.

a.q: Which of these is a major financial decision?
opts: Taking out a loan to buy a first car
Buying a new water bottle for school
Choosing a snack at the canteen
Paying for a bus ticket to a friend's house
a.why: A car loan costs a lot, lasts for years and is hard to undo. The other three cost little and are easy to replace or repeat.
a.clue: Which one will affect your money for years?

b.q: Zara has $15 spare and sees a game she likes. Her brother Sam is deciding whether to sign a three-year lease on a flat. Why does Sam's decision need more planning?
opts: It costs more, lasts longer and is harder to undo
It is made by an adult, so it must be harder
It involves a flat, and flats are always expensive
It will be made only once, so planning is optional
b.why: Sam's lease commits him to a large cost for years, and leaving early is hard. Zara's $15 game is cheap, so a poor choice costs little. Who makes the choice does not decide how much planning it needs.
b.clue: Compare the cost and how easy each choice is to undo.

a.best: Taking out a loan to buy a first car

b.best: It costs more, lasts longer and is harder to undo

problems.detail: All three wrong options carry absolute words ('only', 'must', 'always'), and the right option is the only one without them. A test-wise student can pick it without knowing the idea. Reword the distractors so they are plausible without absolutes.
The clue 'Compare the cost and how easy each choice is to undo' nearly restates the right option ('costs more ... harder to undo'), so it gives the answer away.

check.summary: The card, the remember line and question a are sound. Question b gives its answer away: the distractors all use absolute words ('only', 'must', 'always') while the right option does not, and the clue nearly restates the right option.
